svg.title: What has to fit inside 24 GB
svg.desc: Four horizontal bars against a dashed 24 gigabyte budget line. Two-bit weights for 74 billion parameters take 18.5 gigabytes. A 256K-token key-value cache costs 80 gigabytes on a dense 70-billion-parameter geometry, 22 gigabytes if all 88 layers were attention layers with two key-value heads at bf16, and 4 gigabytes with roughly 32 attention layers at int8. Only the last of the three cache figures leaves room beside the weights, which is why a hybrid backbone with two key-value heads is what makes a 24 gigabyte budget and a 256K context compatible.
svg.text: Gigabytes that must share one 24 GB card
KV cache at 256K — dense 70B-class geometry (80 layers, 8 KV heads, bf16)
KV cache at 256K — if all 88 layers were attention, 2 KV heads, bf16
KV cache at 256K — ~32 attention layers, 2 KV heads, int8
Weights plus cache must fit together. Only the bottom row leaves room beside 18.5 GB of weights — which is
what a hybrid Mamba-attention backbone with two KV heads buys, and what it charges for in recall.
